answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks through linked peer endorsement: every new identity must be vouched for by established agents, and each endorser posts a bond burned if the endorsed agent proves fraudulent. Because trust flows through a sparse contact graph, an attacker must persuade many well-connected agents to stake collateral, and one bad seed taints its whole branch, so costs compound along every forged relationship. Vouching records stay sealed in an audit vault, reviewers trace each lineage back to its ember, and old sybil clusters decay toward the horizon as bonds drain.
